description: A Chinese-language six-player, host-led print-and-play mystery built around a fair reversal where character statements remain literally true.
scope_audience: The stated scope is a complete 150–180 minute game for six players plus a host, with role booklets, host manual, clue cards, solution/specification, and a spoiler-safe front door. It is an entertainment/demo artifact, not game software.

creativity.reason: The truth-only, assumption-driven misdirection thesis is an interesting, clearly articulated design constraint; no public comparison establishes global novelty.

current_usefulness.reason: The materials and seven-stage host flow form a plausible table-ready experience, but the recorded playthroughs are agent blind tests, not real-table validation.

expected_usefulness.reason: A successful fair-play mystery is a concrete entertainment outcome for a named group; its appeal and clue fairness remain untested with human players.

impl_progress.reason: The inspected specification and host manual connect the premise to clue rounds, voting, and a reveal; two agent blind-test records exist, but they do not satisfy the README’s suggested human-table validation.

presentability.reason: The README gives player/host counts, duration, preparation steps and spoiler boundaries, and directs the host to an actionable manual; no visual print-layout review was done.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The print materials and host procedure are present and described as a completed POC; remaining uncertainty is player response, not missing implementation scope.

contribution: A fully specified, spoiler-conscious mystery whose reversal is intended to come from player assumptions rather than hidden or false clues. The notable locally supported contribution is the end-to-end pairing of that constraint with host rules and an auditable clue/reveal structure.
alternatives_question: Which print-and-play mysteries use truth-only clues and assumption-driven reversals, and how do human tables compare on fair inference, pacing and host burden?
reason: The completed paper-game slice and its distinctive design thesis merit a user-facing trial; the recorded agent simulations must not be presented as human playtest evidence.
next_step: Run one human table with the intended group and record whether players infer the solution from disclosed facts without host rescue; review print usability separately.
